historical_record.description: Under the 1947 recreation bond program the Recreation Commission engaged William G. Merchant, architect, to design a field house at Ocean View Playground, on the block of Plymouth, Lobos, Capitol and Montana.
The Recreation Commission awarded one $842,000 contract to Carrico & Gautier to build four recreation centers: Potrero Hill, Ocean View, St. Mary's and Sunset.

Ocean View Playground and center, Plymouth Avenue and Lobos Street, was dedicated, according to the official list of 1947 recreation bond playgrounds the Recreation and Park Commission entered in its minutes.

The Recreation and Park Commission gave conceptual approval to a $348,000 Open Space renovation of Ocean View Playground and Recreation Center, whose community meetings had asked above all for better lighting and a renovated children's play area.

The Playground Commission bought more Ocean View Playground land for $20,119.50 ($82,731.78 for the 10.28 acres so far), wrecked twenty-six run-down buildings, sold three, built two tennis courts and a basketball court, and fitted an old building as a temporary field house.
The Board of Supervisors bought the first Ocean View Playground land, at Capitol and Plymouth Avenues and Montana and Lobos Streets, for the Playground Commission.
